models.title: Price-to-book-equity ratio
models.summary: The sampling-bias discussion defines P/B as a company share market price divided by book equity per share.

relationship.original_equation: P/B=share market price/book equity per share
relationship.locator: Market to Book Ratio Formula, share-price/net-book-value-per-share equation
relationship.translation_notes: The two currency/share ports cancel to a dimensionless multiple. Market cap/book equity is equivalent only if share/equity attribution and share counts match. It is distinct from forwardP/E because its denominator is a point-in-time book-equity stock,not future earnings flow. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.definition: Nonnegative market price per share at the declared date
variables.context: Same entity,currency,share class and share-count basis; market-price date and book-equity measurement/publication dates explicitly declared

variables.definition: Nonzero book equity attributable to that share class per matching share
variables.context: Same entity,currency,share class and share-count basis; market-price date and book-equity measurement/publication dates explicitly declared

variables.definition: Signed price relative to matching book equity per share
variables.context: Same entity,currency,share class and share-count basis; market-price date and book-equity measurement/publication dates explicitly declared

assumptions: Market price and book equity per share use the same currency,share class,share adjustments and entity scope.
Application boundary: nonnegative price and nonzero book equity per share; positive-book interpretation additionally needs positivebook equity.
For backtests use book-equity data only after the actual publication date; fiscal period-end is not an information-availability date.
limitations: Book equity is an accounting measurement,not a guaranteed liquidation price or intrinsic value.
Zero book equity makes the ratio undefined;negative book equity changes interpretation.
No valuation or trading recommendation follows from the quotient.
